hook: Could a single volcanic eruption 27 million years ago change the Arizona landscape forever?

sections.voiceover: Could a single volcanic eruption 27 million years ago change the Arizona landscape forever?

Chiricahua National Monument features rhyolite pinnacles created 27 million years ago by a massive volcanic eruption. The Turkey Creek caldera, a massive volcanic crater, grew just miles beneath the Arizona surface.
However, these violent eruptions began 26.9 million years ago, spewing ash across the desert landscape.
The volcano blasted 100 cubic miles of volcanic material across the land. These spires rise hundreds of feet within the Chiricahua Mountains Sky Island Complex in Arizona.
These stone sentinels remain 27 million years after the eruption.
